purpose: Deferiprone is used to remove extra iron from your body that builds up over time, especially in people who need frequent blood transfusions, such as those with thalassemia. Too much iron in your body can damage your heart, liver, and other organs. This medicine helps your body get rid of that excess iron through your urine.
how_it_works: When you get many blood transfusions, iron from those transfusions builds up in your body because your body has no natural way to remove it. Deferiprone works like a magnet — it grabs onto the excess iron in your body and binds to it tightly. Once attached, the iron is carried out of your body when you urinate, helping keep your iron levels at a safer level.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, and loss of appetite are the most common side effects, especially when you first start the medicine. Your urine may turn reddish or brownish — this is normal and just means the medicine is working and removing iron. Joint pain is also sometimes reported.
warnings: The most serious warning is that deferiprone can cause a dangerous drop in white blood cells called agranulocytosis, which makes it very hard for your body to fight infections. You will need regular blood tests — usually weekly — to check your white blood cell count. Contact your doctor right away if you develop a fever, chills, sore throat, or signs of infection. Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as it can harm the baby.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is about 25 mg per kilogram of your body weight, taken three times a day with or without food, for a total daily dose of around 75 mg per kilogram. Your doctor will calculate the exact dose based on your weight and how well your body tolerates it. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
